Send Water Report for Technical Review Related knowledge guides Direct answer Industrial wastewater reuse must begin with the origin and variability of the stream, not with a membrane product list. UF can reduce suspended and colloidal loads, NF can provide selective dissolved-species separation, and RO can support broader dissolved-salt reduction. A project may combine these categories, but only after organics, oils, metals, hardness, silica, oxidants, biological activity, pH, temperature and cleaning constraints are understood. Yuchen Water supplies membrane materials and can support the related equipment discussion after the wastewater report and reuse target are reviewed. The buyer problem to solve Industrial wastewater is shaped by the process that created it. Rinse water, cooling-tower blowdown, food-processing wastewater, textile streams and mixed factory effluent can have very different foulants and variability. A single laboratory sample may miss production campaigns, cleaning events or accidental discharges, so the report should describe both normal and peak conditions. Reuse quality must be tied to a destination. Water returned to washing, cooling, boiler preparation or a sensitive production step may require different controls. The project brief should explain where the treated water goes, which constituents create risk there and how concentrate or reject streams will be handled. Report requirements A useful report combines laboratory data with operating context. Values should identify the sampling point, units, test date and whether they represent normal, minimum or peak conditions. Where the stream changes with season or production activity, provide the range instead of one convenient value. process origin and stream segregation normal, minimum and peak flow TDS, conductivity, pH and temperature ranges COD, TOC, oils, surfactants and color where relevant turbidity, suspended solids and biological indicators hardness, alkalinity, silica, metals and scale-forming ions oxidants, solvents or cleaning chemicals reuse target, runtime, existing treatment and concentrate constraints How the membrane category is considered The category decision should explain what the membrane is expected to retain, what may pass, what risks must be controlled upstream and what the downstream process requires. It should also identify uncertainty rather than convert missing data into a confident product claim. UF is often considered as a barrier for particles, colloids and biological solids before a tighter membrane stage. NF may be useful when selective removal or retention serves the reuse objective. RO may be needed when dissolved-salt reduction is central. This functional description does not mean that every wastewater should pass through all three categories. The design must account for changes in feed chemistry and the consequences of concentration. Substances that appear manageable in the feed can become limiting near the concentrate side. Pilot testing or additional analysis may be appropriate for complex streams. The membrane category, loading and cleaning plan should follow evidence rather than a generic reuse flow diagram. Pretreatment and equipment context Pretreatment can involve equalization, oil removal, biological treatment, clarification, media filtration, activated carbon, UF, softening, dosing and cartridge filtration. The order depends on the contaminant profile and the downstream membrane. Equalization and source control can be as important as the filter technology because they reduce shock loads. Instrumentation should detect the variables most likely to damage the membrane or upset product quality. Cleaning access, chemical compatibility, flushing and safe shutdown procedures must be designed around the real stream. Equipment technical support can help match pumps, housings, controls and pretreatment components to the selected membrane category. For difficult organics, solvents, high temperatures or rapidly changing production streams, the recommendation may require additional tests or pilot evidence. documents.text: Report-driven membrane knowledge Vontron Membrane Knowledge Center: RO, NF and UF Applications Yuchen Water is a Vontron membrane distributor and dealer. We supply membrane materials for residential, commercial and industrial projects and provide related equipment technical support. This center explains membrane categories and applications without asking buyers to select a product model. A current water or process-fluid report, treatment target and operating brief come first. Send Water Report for Technical Review Related knowledge guides From report to ongoing support Water or process-fluid report Share representative analysis, sampling point and variability. Technical assessment Review contaminants, fouling and scaling risks, target quality, output and operating conditions. Membrane-category recommendation Identify a suitable RO, NF, UF, MBR, SW Series or specialty direction before confirming material. Material and equipment support Confirm current official material information and discuss pretreatment, housings, pumps, filters and controls. Supply and after-sales support Coordinate supply, remote commissioning guidance, operating discussion and replacement planning. Membrane categories by treatment role Membrane categories describe separation roles. They are not substitutes for a water report or a final material recommendation. Membrane categories by treatment role Reverse osmosis (RO) RO is considered when broad dissolved-salt reduction or higher-purity product water is required. Feed chemistry, pressure, pretreatment and concentrate conditions define the practical boundary. Membrane categories by treatment role Nanofiltration (NF) NF can support selective dissolved-species and organic separation. The retained and permeating targets, pH, temperature and cleaning conditions must be stated. Membrane categories by treatment role Ultrafiltration (UF) and MBR UF and MBR roles commonly focus on suspended, colloidal and biological material. They may be final barriers or pretreatment before tighter membrane stages. Membrane categories by treatment role SW Series and saline-water RO Seawater and brackish-water applications require salinity, ion, temperature, intake, pretreatment and high-pressure-equipment review before material selection. Application paths Start from the source and intended use. Each path leads to a report checklist and a technical discussion, not to an automatic model choice. Seawater and brackish water Review salinity, ions, temperature, intake variability, biological risk, target permeate and concentrate constraints. Groundwater and well water Check hardness, alkalinity, silica, iron, manganese, gases, salinity and locally relevant contaminants. Municipal and drinking-water preparation Confirm disinfectants, organics, hardness, taste objectives, required output and the downstream use. Industrial wastewater reuse Describe the generating process, variability, organics, oils, metals, solids, reuse destination and concentrate handling. High-salinity and ZLD-related support Provide a complete ion balance, minor scale risks, organics, variability and the intended role of the membrane step. Salt-lake brine and lithium-related fluids State the complete composition and separation target. Membrane-material support is not a promise of a complete extraction process or recovery result. Food, beverage, pharmaceutical and special fluids Define retained components, product-quality targets, sanitation, pH, temperature, cleaning and evidence requirements. Residential and light commercial Match inlet water, demand, pressure, purifier architecture, pretreatment and replacement access rather than a capacity label. What to include in the technical brief water source or process-fluid identity and sampling point complete current laboratory report TDS or conductivity and salinity where relevant pH and temperature range major ions, hardness, alkalinity, silica, iron and manganese turbidity, suspended solids, organics and biological indicators target product-water quality or separation objective required output and daily operating hours existing pretreatment and equipment details known cleaning, concentrate or process constraints How Yuchen Water supports the project water-report and process-objective review membrane-category and material recommendation pretreatment and compatible-component discussion membrane housings, pumps, filtration and control support material supply and supporting-document confirmation remote commissioning and operating guidance replacement and spare-material planning Website content provides category-level technical education. A complete report and confirmed operating brief are required before final material, equipment or performance decisions. Yuchen Water does not claim to manufacture Vontron membranes and does not promise flux, recovery, lifetime, selectivity or project results for an unreviewed stream. Send Water Report for Technical Review Send the water or process-fluid report, treatment target, required output and operating conditions. Yuchen Water will review the membrane-category direction, material-supply scope and related equipment-support questions. documents.text: Buyer Guide Water Filter OEM Buyer Guide for Importers and Distributors This guide helps B2B buyers compare filter cartridges, RO water purifiers, commercial reverse osmosis systems and supplier qualification points before placing OEM or ODM orders with a China water filter factory. Request OEM Quote View Products How to Define the Product Scope For private-label water filtration projects, buyers should start with the target application, water source and replacement cycle. A PP melt blown filter cartridge is normally selected for sediment removal, while CTO carbon block and GAC filters are used for chlorine, taste and odor reduction. T33 inline carbon filters are common as the final taste-polishing stage in RO water purifier programs. Residential and light-commercial RO water purifier projects usually require capacity selection, filter-stage matching, housing size, label artwork, carton design and spare filter kits. Industrial reverse osmosis equipment should be defined by feed water quality, pretreatment design, membrane configuration, operating pressure, automation level and expected permeate flow. Supplier Qualification Checklist A reliable OEM water filter supplier should provide clear specifications, production capability, batch inspection process and export packaging support for wholesale water filtration products. Buyers can ask for material declarations, applicable test reports, factory photos, sample approval records and shipping carton information before confirming a purchase order. Certification wording should be checked carefully. Document availability depends on the exact product, order requirement and destination market, so buyers should confirm the applicable files before purchase. Technical Details Buyers Should Compare For cartridges, compare size, micron rating, filter media, end cap type, gasket material, flow rate, service life and packaging method. For RO systems, compare membrane model, pump selection, pressure switch, solenoid valve, controller, voltage, tank option, filter replacement design and after-sales spare parts list. For commercial RO and industrial RO systems, key items include pretreatment tanks, sand filter, activated carbon filter, softening tank, precision filter, high-pressure pump, membrane housing, conductivity meter, automatic control valve, CIP cleaning option and electrical protection. The correct configuration depends on raw water, site conditions and local maintenance capability. OEM/ODM and Export Packaging Yuchen Water supports OEM labels, custom colors, logo printing, filter label design, carton artwork, user manuals, private-label packaging and project-specific configuration. For export orders, buyers should confirm carton size, pallet loading, wooden crate requirement, destination port and document support before production starts. Need help selecting a water filtration product? Send the target product, quantity, destination country and customization requirements. This workshop procedure keeps pore distribution, strength, chlorine reduction performance and OEM dimensions stable for B2B buyers. Procedure Technology QC key points Design of ingredients Ingredients are designed after raw material QC and confirmed against the order formula. Consistent weight and media ratio for each piece. Mixing Large automatic mixers can blend more than 500 kg of raw material in one batch. Consistent density in each carbon block. Filling Automatic filling machines load carbon media into molds with controlled volume. Stable weight for each piece. Pressure forming Semi-automatic pressing gives stable pressure during block forming. Higher density and more even pore structure. Sintering Semi-automatic sintering follows the approved time and temperature curve. Consistent sintering time, temperature and bond strength. Mold unloading Semi-automatic unloading reduces damage after sintering. Higher finished product yield. Cutting Semi-automatic cutting keeps cartridge length consistent. Typical tolerance can be controlled around 0.2 mm. Packing Manual inspection with semi-vacuum packing or export cartons. Products are protected for warehouse and export shipping. Finished Product QC: Sample Design Before mass production, each order is sampled according to company standards or customer requirements. The formula, sintering time, temperature and process parameters are confirmed first. Samples can be checked by aeration testing and repeated pressurization cycle testing so that pore distribution, mechanical strength, chlorine reduction, taste and odor removal performance stay within the agreed specification. Production procedure During production, operators monitor the key equipment parameters, including temperature, frequency, pressure and filling weight. These controls help the carbon block line run steadily and keep each batch suitable for OEM water filter cartridge orders. Finished product testing Finished cartridges are inspected by batch sampling or full inspection according to the order requirement. QC checks look for visible defects, cracks, abnormal weight, unstable pressure drop and filtration performance issues before packing. Typical carbon block performance Available nominal filtration ratings include 0.5, 1, 5 and 10 microns with high dirt holding capacity. Coconut shell activated carbon blocks are designed to reduce chlorine, taste, odor and VOCs, keep low pressure drop, avoid carbon fines release and offer a cost-effective alternative to extruded carbon block filters. Documentation and custom service For projects that require supporting documents, selected materials or products can be validated or tested according to WQA and NSF/ANSI 42 material requirements when applicable and confirmed for the order. OEM clients can request custom carbon blocks with different OD, ID, length, shapes, logo labels and packaging. Coconut shell activated carbon options can be supplied with iodine value above 1000 and methylene blue adsorption above 120 when specified.
